title: First-quadrant finite-diagonal totals have injective terms
statement: Let I be a bicomplex in a Grothendieck abelian category, indexed horizontally by integers and vertically by nonnegative integers. Suppose negative horizontal columns vanish and all terms are injective. Extend vertically by zero using mappedFunctor(identity) [def-sp-cartan-eilenberg-presentation], flip, and totalize. The resulting cochain complex vanishes below zero and all its terms are injective.

source.document: Stacks Project, Derived Categories and Homology

proof.text: The extended flipped bicomplex vanishes when either index is negative. In total degree n use CoreHasTotal with the finite index type of horizontal degrees in [0,n]. The associated coproduct is the full diagonal coproduct because the omitted terms are zero. Each summand is isomorphic to an original injective term by extendXIso. Finite biproducts of injectives are injective. In negative total degree every summand is zero; total.hom_ext proves the total term is zero.

lean.statement:
theorem cartanEilenberg_total_injective_terms
    {A : Type u} [Category.{v} A] [Abelian A] [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{v} A]
    (I : HomologicalComplex₂ A (ComplexShape.up ℤ) (ComplexShape.up ℕ))
    (hzero : ∀ p : ℤ, p < 0 → IsZero (I.X p))
    (hterms : ∀ (p : ℤ) (r : ℕ), Injective ((I.X p).X r)) :
    let J := ((CartanEilenbergPresentation.mappedFunctor (𝟭 A)).obj I).flip
    CochainComplex.IsStrictlyGE (J.total (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) 0 ∧
      (∀ n, Injective ((J.total (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).X n))
